title: Lemborexant vs Clonidine vs Sedatives to Treat Insomnia in Chronic Pain Patients
official: Lemborexant vs Clonidine vs Zopiclone vs Other Sedatives for Managing Chronic Insomnia in Chronic Pain Patients
summary: Prospective observational crossover study of 250 adults undergoing chronic pain management. For insomnia treatment, patients alternate their usual prescribed sedative versus Lemborexant or Clonidine; on alternate nights. Patients use a validated smartwatch and a validated sleep diary to collect data including mood score, sleep score, sleep duration, and adverse effects. Patients complete the diary for 20-25 days. Pain and mood are measured using numeric rating scales. Sleep score is measured using the Likert sleep scale. Within-patient differences are analyzed. Any change in pain, mood, or sleep scores by 2-points is considered significant.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* adult chronic pain patients
* good treatment compliance
* severe chronic insomnia
* failure of non-pharmacologic sleep therapy
* regular night sedative therapy for 3 months or more
* regular sleep diary
* regular pain and mood diary
* informed consent for diary review
* consent for clinical record quality assurance review

Exclusion Criteria:

* obstructive sleep apnoea
* body mass index (BMI) ≥40
* organ insufficiency
* cognitive disorder
* inability to provide consent
* major neuropsychiatric disorder
* unreliable diary
* cannabis use
* regular alcohol intake
* stimulant use
* substance abuse
* poor treatment compliance
* high dose opioid
* gabapentinoid use
* other sedative use
* mild insomina
* irregular sedative intake
* regular sedative therapy for less than 3 months
* previous adverse/allergic reactions to clonidine or zopiclone
